item.title: Cowboys defense had "heart to heart" players meeting on Monday morning
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Cowboys are taking steps on multiple fronts as they try to improve on a defense that has underperformed through the first five games of the season.
item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys are taking steps on multiple fronts as they try to improve on a defense that has underperformed through the first five games of the season.

Longtime NFL defensive coordinator Mike Pettine is joining the staff and defensive coordinator Christian Parker will be shifting to the booth after coaching from the sideline during the team's 2-3 start. The team's players also had what linebacker DeMarvion Overshown called a "heart to heart" meeting about what they need to do to improve on the field.

"Looking ourselves in the mirror," Overshown said, via the team's website. "Putting what we wanted our standard to be, we put that on the board. We went by bullet point, bullet point. Are we holding up to this? Are we being this? As a unit, how can we get closer? What is it? Just hearing from all of us. It really wasn't like a fire drill conversation, it was more so, 'What can I do to help you? What do I expect from you on Sundays, or every Monday walk throughs?' We've got to talk to each other like that because the ship is only going to go as far as the weakest person on the boat. As long as we all in this together, I think we're going to be great. I know we're going to be there."

Overshown has missed four games with a hamstring injury and his return to health could be another piece of the puzzle as the Cowboys look for the right mix of planning and execution that can turn things around on the defensive side of the ball.

item.title: Report: NFL considers flexing Eagles-Commanders out of prime time
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: As the NFL season begins to take shape, the league office has a growing body of evidence to inform potential flex decisions.
item.content:encoded:
As the NFL season begins to take shape, the league office has a growing body of evidence to inform potential flex decisions. And one game has emerged as a candidate to be the first to exit its current prime-time slot.

Via Rob Tornoe of the Philadelphia Inquirer, the NFL is considering moving the Week 8 game between the Eagles and Commanders out of the Sunday night window.

Plenty of factors influence the NFL's decision-making process. One obvious factor becomes the game that would replace it.

In Week 8, it may not be easy to find a game that would attract a larger audience, even if the Commanders lose to the 49ers on Monday night and fall to 1-4-1 and if the Eagles lose to the Panthers on Sunday and slump to 2-4.

Given the apparent rule that at least one game in each division rivalry must be televised in a Sunday afternoon window, Vikings-Lions, Browns-Steelers, and Chiefs-Broncos would seem to be off limits. Steelers-Browns (Week 4) and Broncos-Chiefs (Week 4) previously were televised in prime time, and the Vikings are scheduled to host the Lions on Sunday night in Week 15.

Of course, the league could decide to take the earlier Vikings-Lions game, with a flex of the Week 15 game in Minneapolis into an afternoon window.

Ravens-Bills becomes a possibility, but the Ravens also play the following Thursday night. The league may not want to give the Ravens seven fewer hours or so between games on a short week.

Colts-Jaguars is a possibility; the Jaguars are 4-1 and the Colts should move to 3-3 this weekend with a home game against the 0-5 Titans. The league would need to consider whether Eagles-Commanders would carry extra national sizzle than Colts-Jaguars even if both Philadelphia and Washington lose this weekend.

Ultimately, the outcomes of this weekend's games will influence the final decision. For now, the Inquirer reports that the possibility of an Eagles-Commanders flex is on the radar screen. The deadline arrives on Tuesday, October 20 — the day after Week 6 ends with the Commanders facing the 49ers in Santa Clara.

item.title: Report: Lamar Jackson has a "realistic chance" to return Week 6
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: On Monday, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter told reporters that quarterback Lamar Jackson was "definitely doing better" after missing Week 5 with an ankle injury.
item.content:encoded:
On Monday, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter told reporters that quarterback Lamar Jackson was "definitely doing better" after missing Week 5 with an ankle injury.

Now there's an indication he may be back after being sidelined for just one game.

Jackson has a "realistic chance" to play against the Browns on Sunday, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Jackson did not practice last week, but Minter has praised the quarterback for doing everything he can to get back as quickly as possible.

In four games so far this season, Jackson has completed 70.8 percent of his passes for 967 yards with six touchdowns and one interception. He’s also rushed for 144 yards with a TD.

Jackson did not practice last week. The Ravens' first injury report of Week 6 is due out later on Wednesday.

item.title: James Thrash upholds Dre Greenlaw suspension for head-butting incident
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The 49ers won't have linebacker Dre Greenlaw for Monday night's game against the Commanders.
item.content:encoded:
The 49ers won't have linebacker Dre Greenlaw for Monday night's game against the Commanders.

The NFL has announced that hearing officer James Thrash, a former NFL receiver, has upheld the one-game suspension imposed Monday on Greenlaw.

During the second quarter of Sunday's game between the 49ers and Seahawks, Greenlaw applied a head butt to Seahawks linebacker Ernest Jones IV. Greenlaw was wearing a helmet; Jones was not.

Greenlaw was ejected. It was his third ejection since 2022. Last year, he was suspended for one game for his behavior toward referee Brad Allen after a game between the Giants and Broncos, Greenlaw's team in 2025.

Greenlaw will forfeit $136,388 in base salary for the game. He'll also lose a $23,529 active roster bonus. The 49ers could be able to seek partial repayment of his $2.5 million signing bonus, too.

The lost reps also will make it harder for Greenlaw to earn a $750,000 incentive based on 75-percent playing time for the season. If earned, the amount doubles if the 49ers make the playoffs.

item.title: It's official: Rams LT Alaric Jackson suspended two games
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The NFL has made the two-game suspension of Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson official.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL has made the two-game suspension of Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson official.

Jackson is set to miss games against the Cardinals and Raiders.

He can appeal, with either Derrick Brooks, Jordy Nelson, Ron Rivera or James Thrash hearing Jackson's appeal and rendering a decision.

Jackson threw a right hook to Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb after the Rams’ 37-34 overtime loss on Monday night.

ESPN’s cameras caught Jackson exchanging jerseys with Bills defensive lineman Deone Walker at midfield when Chubb appeared to say something to Jackson. Jackson punched Chubb in the face with his right hand before Rams tight end Colby Parkinson pulled Jackson away.

Chubb called it “just emotions” after the game.

Jackson has started all five games this season and missed only one game last season.

item.title: Joe Brady wishes he'd taken two knees before Monday night's game-winning field goal
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Week 5 included plenty of examples of how not to best manage the clock in late-game situations.
item.content:encoded:
Week 5 included plenty of examples of how not to best manage the clock in late-game situations. Most of the coaches who learned lessons did so the hard way, by losing their games.

Bills coach Joe Brady learned a lesson while still winning.

In a Tuesday session with reporters, Brady expressed regret for attempting the game-winning 45-yard field goal on second down, with two minutes left in overtime.

"I didn't want to run two QB sneaks with the fall process of, again, getting — putting the ball in harm's way, taking some shots on Josh, just to get — we knew we were already in line," Brady said. "So it's like, hey, do I just, hey, center the ball and just take two knees? You know, you go back two yards, but you don't give them, you know, they end up worse if you miss. They get 45 seconds to, you know, to go 20 yards for the field goal. Big difference in two-minute, and, you know, the 45-yard field goal and a 47-yard field goal percentages, you should still be good to go, right?

"And, you know, so if I had that opportunity again — look, I was convicted about it. You know, [Tyler Bass] was good to go. The conversation we had in the huddle and upstairs was like, 'Let's just go win the game right now.' But, you know, to not give them that shot again, if we do miss, the best thing would be is to take two knees and say, 'Hey, the 45 and the 47 is not of big difference.' Be a completely different story if the ball was a little further back. I'd be no indecision on taking knees if we were a little closer. We were just in that. It is a long field goal. We had just missed an extra point, but had the confidence in [Bass], but that's when I do wish I probably took two knees, and then we kicked the game winner. And if anything, they'd have 45 seconds and not two minutes."

Plenty of Bills fans would surely prefer a 45-yard field goal try to a 47-yard field goal attempt. For obvious reasons. Regardless, the thought process is another example of the decisions coaches need to make in real time, with the clock ticking.

If the kick had missed from 47, the Rams would have had less than 40 seconds to gain enough ground to try another potential game-winner. A miss from 45 would have given the Rams triple that amount of time.

item.title: Joe Brady: James Cook's ball security has to improve or carries will decrease
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: James Cook ran for 111 yards and two touchdowns against the Rams on Monday night, but a negative play almost became his lasting memory of the game.
item.content:encoded:
James Cook ran for 111 yards and two touchdowns against the Rams on Monday night, but a negative play almost became his lasting memory of the game.

Cook fumbled just outside the Rams' 20-yard-line a couple of minutes into overtime and the Rams recovered to give themselves a chance to win the game. Greg Rousseau blocked a field goal attempt, however, and the Bills were able to drive for a kick of their own.

Tyler Bass made that kick and the Bills won 37-34, but head coach Joe Brady said on Tuesday that the outcome does not overshadow all that happened to get to that point. Cook's fumble was his second of the night, fourth of the season and his 11th dating back to the start of the 2025 season. He's also run for a league-high 2,153 yards over that span, but Brady made it clear that the ball has to stop squirting out of his hands.

“He's doing so many good things running the football," Brady said. "I don't want to lose sight of how great he is running the ball right now. But putting the ball on the ground, it's negating all the positive. I have all the confidence in him. That's why I put him right back out there. But obviously, at some point there has to be consequences to when we're putting negative stuff out there .The conversations that we’re having ongoing, James knows it’s important. It's going to cost us football games. It almost cost us one. We can't confuse because we won the game that that's OK. It's got to improve or the carries are going to decrease."

Brady noted that Josh Allen also threw an interception on Monday and said the team is generally "putting the ball in harm's way" too often. They got a painful lesson about how that can hurt a team's chances of winning in Denver during the playoffs last season and Brady would like to see his team avoid any similar outcomes in big moments this season.

item.title: PFT's Week 6 2026 NFL power rankings
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Niners hold the top spot.
item.content:encoded:
1. 49ers (last week No. 1; 5-0): Plenty of other teams wish they'd made a run at signing Mike Evans.

2. Chiefs (No. 2; 4-0): They've got a chance to deliver the death blow to the Chargers' season.

3. Jaguars (No. 3; 4-1): On a Sunday that featured plenty of lessons, Jacksonville's contribution was to highlight the importance of having a backup long snapper.

4. Bills (No. 4; 3-1): Joe Brady wasn't going to eff around and find out by trying to get the game-winning field goal closer.

5. Seahawks (No. 5; 3-2): They're trying too hard to be something other than they were in 2025.

6. Vikings (No. 8; 5-0): As the offense improves, the Vikings go from "contender" to "threat."

7. Broncos (No. 6; 3-2): When Seattle comes to town on Thursday night, everyone will find out whether this team is a true candidate to get to the Super Bowl.

8. Ravens (No. 10; 4-1): The Ravens still look like the Ravens, even after a coaching change.

9. Patriots (No. 13; 3-2): The patriotic pigeons had a field day on Tom Brady's statue.

10. Rams (No. 7; 2-3): They have five winnable games before the bye; if they lose any of them, things could get interesting down the stretch.

11. Packers (No. 23; 3-2): When your adversary keeps talking, stay quiet and wait for your opportunity.

12 (tie). Browns (No. 12; 3-2): They're first in the list because they beat the Steelers.

12 (tie). Steelers (No. 14; 3-2): They're second in the list because they beat the Bengals.

12 (tie). Bengals (No. 15; 3-2): The win over the Dolphins shouldn't have come down to an onside kick.

15. Bears (No. 9; 3-2): Tyson Bagent's expiration date seems to have arrived.

16. Raiders (No. 11; 3-2): At what point will Fernando Mendoza become the better option to lead a run to a possible playoff berth?

17. Giants (No. 16; 3-1-1): Dan Quinn saved John Harbaugh and Cam Skattebo from being the pin cushions of talk radio in New York.

18. Panthers (No. 19; 2-2): They could win the division by default, again.

19. Eagles (No. 17; 2-3): A bad week ended in the worst way possible.

20. Cowboys (No. 18; 2-3): The arrival of Mike Pettine is both an acknowledgement that the defense needs help and a failure to acquire the kind of help it needs.

21. Lions (No. 21; 3-2): Nothing helps a bad defense like playing a bad offense.

22. Falcons (No. 20; 2-3): Michael Penix Jr. has a long way to go to show that he's sufficiently durable to be a franchise quarterback.

23. Colts (No. 22; 2-3): It feels like an overhaul is inevitable.

24. Texans (No. 24; 1-4): They still have a long way to go to become the team that they were in 2025.

25. Saints (No. 25; 1-4): Three straight home losses may be very hard to overcome.

26. Jets (No. 28; 2-3): Geno Smith has gone from leading the league in interceptions to throwing none.

27. Buccaneers (No. 30; 1-4): They may have found something in Jalon Daniels.

28. Commanders (No. 26; 1-3-1): The clock is still ticking on Dan Quinn. In more ways than one.

29. Cardinals (No. 27; 1-4): The Week 1 win over the Chargers becomes less impressive by the week.

30. Chargers (No. 29; 0-5): The price for a potential Justin Herbert trade is dropping by the week.

31. Titans (No. 31; 0-5): The constant turnover in the organization feels like Game of Thrones meets the Island of Misfit Toys.

32. Dolphins (No. 32; 0-5): Maybe Jon-Eric Sullivan and Jeff Hafley should have waited a year.

item.title: Matt LaFleur on Micah Parsons: As soon as they give us the green light, he'll be out there
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Earlier in the day, reporting out of ESPN indicated Packers edge rusher Micah Parsons is not expected to return to practice this week as he continues to recover from a torn ACL suffered late last season.
item.content:encoded:
Earlier in the day, reporting out of ESPN indicated Packers edge rusher Micah Parsons is not expected to return to practice this week as he continues to recover from a torn ACL suffered late last season.

In his Monday press conference, Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur confirmed that will be the case.

“Soon as they give us the green light, he’ll be out there,” LaFleur said. “So, that hasn’t happened yet. But I think we’re getting closer.

“There’s a lot of testing that goes on before he gets medically cleared to get out there,” LaFleur added. “And then I’m sure we’re going to want to give him some time to get back to playing football. As you see with most guys who are coming off a major injury, it takes a little bit of time.”

That means Parsons will not be back in time to face the team that traded him, as the Packers will play the Cowboys on Sunday night this week.

LaFleur noted the team wants to make sure Parsons is in the best spot possible when he comes back.

“I mean, he’s a physical specimen. He’s a creature of nature, for sure,” LaFleur said. “And sometimes, you’ve got to make sure that your body is [in sync]. … You don’t want one leg to be that much stronger than the other leg, is what I’m getting at.”

The Packers play the Cowboys at home on Sunday, the Lions on the road in Week 7, and then come home to play the Panthers on Thursday night in Week 8. They have a game on the road against the Patriots in Week 9 and a home matchup against the Vikings in Week 10 before a Week 11 bye.

item.title: Dealing with blood clots in lung left Taylor Moton with "attitude of gratitude" for chance to return
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Panthers offensive tackle Taylor Moton began "thinking the worst" when he coughed up blood in June and a trip to the hospital showed that he had "a multitude of clots" in his right lung.
item.content:encoded:
Panthers offensive tackle Taylor Moton began "thinking the worst" when he coughed up blood in June and a trip to the hospital showed that he had "a multitude of clots" in his right lung.

Moton was put on a course of blood thinners for three months and he was prohibited from playing football during that time, so he has been on the non-football injury list since the start of training camp. Moton completed that treatment and has been told by doctors that he has a "relatively low" chance of dealing with more blood clots in the future, which has opened the door to a return to the field.

Moton's first step was returning to practice on Tuesday and he broke the team down at the end of the workout. His message was one of thanks for being able to resume his career and continue living his life.

"My message today was, guys, just have an attitude of gratitude," Moton said, via the team's website. "Coach [Dave] Canales spoke on that too, man, and that's just not taking it for granted, you know what I mean? And along with that is just making sure we come in here and you come to work, you do everything the right way, right? You put 100 percent effort and all your preparation, and that's not just in the building; that's out of the building with watching film, how you hydrate with your nutrition, with your treatment routine, whatever that is, sticking with that plan, man. And ultimately just that that's how you show gratitude for this because you never know when that day comes. Honestly, it gave me more gratitude for life in general. Like football, yeah. But just past that, just now I wake up with a new sense of happy to be able to put my feet on this side of the Earth."

Moton doesn't know if he will be playing against the Eagles this week, but having the chance to play again at any point is a win after a summer of uncertainty on all fronts.

item.title: Rams move on from K Harrison Mevis, sign K Blake Grupe
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Rams have completed at least one part of their evaluation of special teams.
item.content:encoded:
The Rams have completed at least one part of their evaluation of special teams.

According to a report from NFL Network, Los Angeles is releasing kicker Harrison Mevis and signing kicker Blake Grupe off of the Jets' practice squad.

In Monday night's loss to the Bills, Mevis missed a field goal and had his 48-yard attempt to win the game in overtime blocked.

He also missed a field goal against Philadelphia in Week 4 and one against the Giants in Week 2.

Grupe lost his job with the Saints after missing several field goals in 2025. But he made all 11 of his field goals and all 10 of his extra points in five games with the Colts late in the year.

The Rams have been through several kickers and special teams coordinators in recent years, with a notable lack of success on the unit. If the club is going to turn its 2-3 start into postseason contention, the field goal operation will need to be more consistently successful.

item.title: Micah Parsons: "Jayden Daniels probably cost Dan Quinn his job"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Packers LB minces no words about QB's role in clock disaster.
item.content:encoded:
Micah Parsons still isn't ready to play after last year's knee injury, but he still knows how to mix things up.

Parsons recently said on his podcast, The Edge with Micah Parsons, that quarterback Jayden Daniels is to blame for the game-clock clusterfudge at the end of overtime in the Giants-Commanders game.

"Jayden Daniels probably cost my man Dan Quinn his job, to be honest with you," Parsons said, via Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic. "To be honest with you. And, like, I'm a big Jayden Daniels fan. But the reality is, he probably cost a lot of people their jobs this past weekend. . . .

"All respectfully, we get coached so much on these situations that, like, I'm a defensive player, and this shit's programmed to me. I even know what to do in those situations. There's no way I'm taking a sack with 14 seconds left and no timeouts. . . . And, mind you, it'd be different if Jayden Daniels was a rookie. This is your third year. This is your third year. You've been to the NFC Championship game. You've been in big moments before. And to me, like even after a sack, you're casually getting up."

Parsons made it clear that, in his view, quarterbacks are expected to always know what's going on.

"This is your job, bro," Parsons said. "This is your job to be prepared to understand the game and understand situations. That's in your job profile. And you're telling me, 'Oh, we're gonna want to pay this guy eventually $60 million? This cannot happen. . . . I'm a big JD5 fan, but that's inexcusable, bro."

Parsons said that the Packers work on situational football "every day," What happened at the end of the Giants-Commanders game should have required no discussion, frankly.

"This is a lack of preparation, a lack of mentality, and a lack of urgency," Parsons said. "That just can't happen."

Parsons isn't wrong. The fact that it did happen raises plenty of questions about the level of preparation and attention to detail, as created by the coaching staff. It speaks to potential cultural flaws, perhaps one in which Daniels hasn't been challenged or held as accountable as he could have or should have been, given his standing in the organization.

It would be a lot easier to make sense of all of this if the Commanders had recorded and preserved the relevant communications. And Daniels surely will face even more questions on this topic the next time he speaks to reporters.

The fact that the outcome was so bizarre, so jarring, and so downright surreal becomes a horrible moment for everyone involved. As to the ultimate consequences, Parsons hit the nail on the head — Daniels's failure to take charge of the situation in the moment will probably cost Quinn his job.

But Daniels will continue to be the starting quarterback because, even if he made an inexcusable mistake as to one of the easiest parts of the job, he does the hard parts better than most of his peers.

item.title: Report: Ja'Kobi Lane is expected to return to practice
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Ravens are getting closer to having one of their key rookies return to play.
item.content:encoded:
The Ravens are getting closer to having one of their key rookies return to play.

Per a report from NFL Network, receiver Ja’Kobi Lane is expected to return to practice on Wednesday.

Lane, a third-round pick in this year’s draft, underwent wrist surgery after going down during the Ravens’ Week 1 victory over the Colts.

He caught one pass for 11 yards in the season opener before his exit.

The Ravens released Chris Moore on Tuesday, an indication of Lane’s potential availability for Sunday’s game against the Browns.

Baltimore’s first injury report of the week is set to be released later in the day.

item.title: President Trump was expected to attend Steelers-Bucs, before his schedule changed
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Commander-in-Chief's propensity to attend sporting events almost resulted in his presence at another NFL game.
item.content:encoded:
The Commander-in-Chief's propensity to attend sporting events almost resulted in his presence at another NFL game. But it ultimately didn't.

On Tuesday, Kristen Holmes of CNN reported that President Trump was expected to attend the Week 6 game between the Steelers and Buccaneers in Tampa. Later in the day, she reported that Trump would not be making the trip.

It would have been the third NFL game attended by Trump during his current term. He was present for Super Bowl LIX in New Orleans between the Chiefs and Eagles. Last year, he attended a Lions-Commanders game in Maryland, making him the first sitting president to attend a regular-season game in nearly 50 years.

Two years ago, in the weeks preceding the election that resulted in his second term, Trump attended a Sunday night game between the Jets and Steelers.

It remains to be seen whether he shows up for an NFL game before the midterm elections, which happen in 20 days. The Commanders are currently scheduled to host the Eagles on Sunday, November 1 — two days before the in-person polls officially open.

item.title: Jesse Minter: Lamar Jackson is "definitely doing better"
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Baltimore's HC said the QB is doing everything he can to get back on the field.
item.content:encoded:
Though they didn't have their starting quarterback, the Ravens were still able to beat the Falcons in overtime to push their record to 4-1 on Sunday night.

Will Lamar Jackson be back for Week 6 against division rival Cleveland?

That's still to be determined.

“[Jackson is] definitely doing better,” head coach Jesse Minter told reporters in his Monday press conference. “Wednesday, I’m not sure exactly how that practice will look. But, again, to Lamar’s credit, he’s doing everything he can to get back out there.”

Jackson suffered an ankle sprain during the Week 4 victory over the Titans. Tyler “Snoop” Huntley started Sunday’s game, going 24-of-32 passing for 201 yards with two touchdowns. He also rushed six times for 20 yards with a TD.

Minter complimented Jackson for how engaged he was on the sideline during the contest.

“I thought [Jackson] was awesome — there’s a lot of cool pictures and clips of him on the sideline in between series, talking to ‘Snoop’ and hyping guys up,” Minter said. “What a wonderful teammate and leader that he is, even when he wasn’t playing. So, very proud of Lamar for handling himself like that.

“And, again, he’s doing everything he can. I think we’ll know more, definitely, by the middle of the week.”

Additionally, Minter noted that center Cam Jurgens is nearing the end of the concussion protocol, which could mean he’s available for this week’s game against the Browns. Receiver Ja'Kobi Lane and outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson also could return for the Week 6 matchup.

item.title: Saints owner Gayle Benson: I won't accept this level of play as our standard
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Seats are starting to heat up in New Orleans.
item.content:encoded:
Seats are starting to heat up in New Orleans.

The Saints lost to the Vikings in Week 5 to fall to 1-4 on the season. The last three losses came in a row and all three came at the Superdome, including a Monday night drubbing at the hands of the Vikings on a night when the Saints celebrated the 20th anniversary of their post-Katrina return to the stadium.

On Tuesday, owner Gayle Benson said that loss "truly disappointed me" during a speech at the Greater New Orleans Quarterback Club Luncheon that left no doubt about how disappointed she is with the team's performance in general. Benson said fans "are right to expect more than we have delivered" through the first five weeks of the season.

“As the owner, the responsibility does start with me,” Benson said, via Rod Walker of NOLA.com. “I will not make excuses and I will not accept this level of performance as our standard. I am committed to making the decisions necessary to improving this team. Everyone on this organization understands the urgency. We must prepare better, execute consistently and correct mistakes that are costing us the games.”

Benson didn't issue any ultimatums about a more acceptable standard of play, but she did vow to hold people accountable if the Saints are not able to right their ship in the coming weeks.

“Kellen Moore and his coaches are responsible for preparing our players to perform," Benson said. "Mickey Loomis and our football staff are responsible for building a roster capable of sustained success. The players are responsible for their preparation and execution. I am responsible for holding this organization accountable.”

Moore is in his second season as the head coach while Loomis has been the General Manager since 2002. The Saints are 7-15 since Moore was hired in 2025 and it sounds like that record will need to get a lot better in order for anyone to feel secure about returning in 2027.

item.title: With Odell Beckham Jr. in Minnesota, Jauan Jennings could be traded
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The 49ers continue to have injury issues at the receiver position.
item.content:encoded:
The 49ers continue to have injury issues at the receiver position. And the Vikings have a current surplus of receivers that includes a player who had spent his first five seasons with the 49ers.

On Tuesday, Ian Rapoport of ESPNFL floated the possibility of Jauan Jennings being traded to the 49ers, in the coming days.

It would not be a surprise. As we explained after the Vikings signed Odell Beckham Jr. last week, OBJ's arrival seemed to be a message to Jennings, who has two catches for nine yards in four 2026 appearances with two starts.

As the Vikings enter their bye, it's a perfect time to assess the roster and to see if any moves can be made, either by adding a player or subtracting one. The Vikings seem to believe Beckham can still play, and the Vikings seem to be perplexed by Jennings's inability to contribute to the passing game.

In lieu of simply cutting Jennings, there's a possible deal to be made that would get the Vikings something of value in exchange for the balance of his one-year contract, which included a $4.5 million signing bonus with a $1.63 million base salary and nearly $100,000 per game in active roster bonuses and incentives tied to playing time and receptions.

If the 49ers are interested in bringing Jennings back, they could wait for the Vikings to potentially release him. But with Deebo Samuel joining the list of the substation's victims (again) with a hamstring injury, time could be of the essence for the 49ers.

Or maybe Jennings gets the wakeup call, and it works. Either way, the clock is ticking. And continuing to hit the snooze button isn't a viable option.

item.title: Seahawks tailoring playbook so Sam Darnold can make "swift decisions," avoid turnovers
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: There are a lot of things that go into winning and losing football games, but a quick glance at the Seahawks' performance in the first five weeks of the season leads to one obvious conclusion about their results.
item.content:encoded:
There are a lot of things that go into winning and losing football games, but a quick glance at the Seahawks' performance in the first five weeks of the season leads to one obvious conclusion about their results.

In their three wins, the Seahawks have turned the ball over twice but they have turned it over seven times in their two losses. Four of those turnovers in the losses have been interceptions thrown by quarterback Sam Darnold — he has five overall — and cutting down on those giveaways is at the top of the to-do list in Seattle heading into Thursday's game against the Broncos.

On Tuesday, offensive coordinator Brian Fleury said that he and Darnold are working to tailor their game plan so that it emphasizes plays that allow Darnold to feel comfortable and decisive on the field.

"It's relying more heavily on plays that we have a lot of experience with both through training camp and through the first couple weeks that he's comfortable making swift decisions and progressing through," Fleury said, via the team's website. "We're going to lean more in that direction."

The Seahawks have had chances to win both games they lost in spite of the turnovers and those chances would be a lot better if they didn't give the ball away, so turning the focus to cutting them out is a prudent response with the race for playoff positioning in the NFC already well underway.

item.title: First-place Giants are a distant third in betting odds to win the NFC East
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: In seven of the NFL's eight divisions, the team that is currently in first place is also currently the betting favorite to win the division.
item.content:encoded:
In seven of the NFL's eight divisions, the team that is currently in first place is also currently the betting favorite to win the division. The NFC East is the exception.

At 3-1-1, the Giants are in first place in the NFC East by 1.5 games. But they're a distant third in the betting odds to win the division.

The betting odds currently list the 2-3 Eagles as the favorites at +170, followed closely by the 2-3 Cowboys at +180. The Giants are third at +320, and the 1-3-1 Commanders are last at +750.

It's not hard to understand why the bettors aren't sold on the Giants: Despite managing to win three games, they haven't looked particularly good while doing so, on either offense or defense. (Their special teams are playing well.) Starting quarterback Jaxson Dart is out for the season and there are doubts about how long they can keep winning with Jameis Winston. And their schedule has been easy; all five teams they've played currently have losing records.

The schedule stays easy this week, with a home game against the 1-4 Saints. The Giants are 1.5-point underdogs, which underscores how little faith the bettors have in them. If the Giants manage to win on Sunday, their odds to win the division may improve a little. But it won't be until November 8, when they travel to Philadelphia to take on the Eagles, when the Giants can make a statement that they really are the best team in the NFC East. Unless the Giants keep winning through that game, they're going to stay long shots to win the division.

item.title: Liam Coen: I can do more to avoid delay of game penalties
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Jaguars were able to take advantage of the Eagles' poor clock management to pull out a win at the end of last Sunday's game in London, but their own miscues cost them a chance to take firmer control of the game earlier in the fourth quarter.
item.content:encoded:
The Jaguars were able to take advantage of the Eagles' poor clock management to pull out a win at the end of last Sunday's game in London, but their own miscues cost them a chance to take firmer control of the game earlier in the fourth quarter.

A Trevor Lawrence pass to tight end Brenton Strange landed the Jaguars at the Eagles' 1-yard-line with under nine minutes to play, but they burned a timeout before getting the next snap off. After a false start and a short run, the Jaguars sandwiched a pair of delay of game penalties around an incompletion and ultimately failed on fourth down to end the drive without any points.

The Jags had another delay of game in the first quarter and head coach Liam Coen said on Wednesday that the penalties were "directly on me." He also explained how he can do more to make sure that the Jaguars don't continue to struggle with getting plays off in time.

"That was probably one of the louder atmospheres I've been in a while," Coen said, via Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com. "Especially in those critical moments to where, 'Hey guys, I can help you out with my playcall.' Maybe shorten it up, trim the verbiage or call something a little bit more simplified down there where it was in that end zone specifically that got loud and some of those critical downs."

The Jaguars had 13 penalties overall against the Eagles and they had 13 more against the Bengals in Week 4. They won that game as well, but the lack of discipline is something that is likely to catch up with them if Coen can't clean up the operation in the coming weeks.

item.title: Brock Purdy will soon be the NFL's all-time leader in career passer rating
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Brock Purdy will have the highest career passer rating in NFL history, just as soon as he has enough pass attempts to qualify for the record.
item.content:encoded:
Brock Purdy will have the highest career passer rating in NFL history, just as soon as he has enough pass attempts to qualify for the record.

Purdy's career passer rating of 105.4 is higher than the official record, which is Lamar Jackson's 102.7. But to qualify for the record, a quarterback needs 1,500 career passing attempts, and Purdy is currently just short, with 1,495 career pass attempts.

So as soon as Purdy throws his fifth pass on Monday night against the Commanders, he'll have the record. Purdy's lead over Jackson is such that even if Purdy were to throw five straight interceptions to start Monday night's game, he'd still have the record: If Purdy throws five picks on his next five passes, his passer rating will fall to 103.7, which is better than Jackson's record.

Passer rating is a fairly goofy statistic which the NFL adopted as its official method for ranking passers in 1973. Its weaknesses as a measurement for a quarterback's quality include overvaluing completion percentage, arbitrarily capping the maximum amount of credit a quarterback can get for a certain statistic, and ignoring important variables like first downs and sacks, not to mention the things beyond passing that a quarterback can do, good or bad, like running the ball or fumbling.

Still, it's a statistic that roughly measures how good a passer a quarterback is, and in the history of the league, it measures Purdy as the best ever.

item.title: Drew Rosenhaus still claims a Tyreek Hill deal "could happen at any time"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Rosenhaus comments on Hill's prospects, without addressing the potential impact of the pending NFL investigation.
item.content:encoded:
Before a civil verdict was entered on Tuesday against free-agent receiver Tyreek Hill, his agent Drew Rosenhaus revisited the question of whether Hill will soon be joining an NFL team.

"I think it’s very fluid," Rosenhaus told Josh Moser of WVSN. "I think a deal could happen any time. We are looking for the right situation, the right contract, the right team, the right fit, the right approach from a medical standpoint. Tyreek's feeling really good health-wise. I did say last week I thought a deal could happen at any time. But in the NFL it really is day-to-day. So we are still working to find the right situation."

What are the factors in finding the right situation?

"Well, you know, when you sign with a team midseason you'd like to go to a winner," Rosenhaus said. "Number two, as a wide receiver, you'd like to go to a team that needs a wide receiver. Number three, you'd like to go to a team that's got a pretty good quarterback. And number four, Tyreek's gonna bring a lot of impact. We've got to get a fair contract. And that's always complex to negotiate in the middle of a season.

"So kind of look at Tyreek as similar to guys that are traded midseason. Can really come in and help a team in the second half of the year. He can help a team advance to the next level."

It's still not clear whether Hill has fully recovered from a serious knee injury that he suffered in September 2025, during the Week 4 Monday night game against the Jets.

"I don't know that he's 100 percent today, but he's close and he'll get there really soon," Rosenhaus said. "But I think that's probably something you have to wait until he gets out in practices and gets with the team before saying he's 100 percent. But he really is right there."

The clip posted online includes no discussion of the pending Personal Conduct Policy investigation, or the potential impact of the then-pending civil trial. With Hill found responsible for two counts of battery, it's a significant complication — both as to how the league will proceed (paid leave becomes a possibility immediately after he signs) and as to whether a team will want to accept the P.R. consequences of adding a player who has just been found liable by a jury for battery of his ex-wife, and ordered to pay her $500,000 in damages.

item.title: Sean McVay on Alaric Jackson: "He has to consistently do a better job"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: On Monday, Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson sucker punched Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb.
item.content:encoded:
On Monday, Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson sucker punched Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb. On Tuesday, the NFL suspended Jackson for two games.

After the suspension was imposed, Rams coach Sean McVay addressed the expectations for Jackson.

“It is very important to represent the things that we want to be about," McVay told reporters. "He has to consistently do a better job. I think each situation is its own separate entity. I think you want to be careful pigeonholing yourself into a one-size-fits-all. The league made their decision. I want to understand the totality of the situation.

"I'm not condoning by any stretch of the imagination, but I want to gather all the information before I make comments. It certainly doesn't help us when we're missing a player of his caliber. He has to make more consistent decisions that are in alignment with being available and representing the things that we want to be about without a doubt."

McVay also explained that David Quesenberry will replace Jackson during the suspension.

McVay, who said he believes Jackson will appeal the decision, doesn't know what Chubb said to prompt the punch from Chubb.

While Chubb's words won't excuse the reaction, California does have a "fighting words" law that prohibits certain comments that are "inherently likely to provoke an immediate reaction." That would be relevant if the local authorities get involved in the situation.

Frankly, they should. The game was over, for several minutes. Jackson's pads were off. He returned to the field for the conversation that led to the altercation. If the situation had unfolded elsewhere and in the presence of a police officer, Jackson would have been (or at least should have been) immediately arrested.

In this case, the evidence is on video. Why shouldn't Jackson be charged with battery? Anyone else who sucker punched someone in a public place would be, or at least should be.

item.title: Dan Campbell says pass protection shows why Jahmyr Gibbs is different from other backs
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Gibbs made the key block on a touchdown pass from Jared Goff to Sam LaPorta on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs set the NFL record for most touchdowns before turning 25 on Sunday. But Lions coach Dan Campbell says it was a teammate's touchdown that showed what a special player Gibbs is.

On a fourth-and-1 touchdown pass from Jared Goff to Sam LaPorta, Gibbs made the key block in pass protection that gave Goff time to pass. Campbell said after watching the film he sought Gibbs out to praise his blocking on that play.

"I hit him up this morning," Campbell said. "I said, one of my favorite clips of everything you did — he had a ton of eye-opening plays — was his his protection route on the fourth-and-1, LaPorta's touchdown. That was outstanding. To me, that's why he's different. All this other stuff, of course he's got that and it's rare. It's that. He's unselfish and he's tough and he's willing to do anything for his teammates. And he might as well have scored on that because he's as excited as anybody is that he helped get LaPorta a touchdown and protect Goff so he could make that throw. That's unselfishness."

Gibbs ran for 151 yards and caught five passes for 56 yards against the Cardinals, and he's currently leading the NFL with 747 yards from scrimmage and nine touchdowns. But Gibbs makes highlight-reel plays even when he doesn't have the ball in his hands.

item.title: Bo Nix: Playing good and playing bad, it’s a narrative and something made up
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Bo Nix dismisses the numbers.
item.content:encoded:
Bo Nix dismisses the numbers.

The Broncos' quarterback seemingly has had a pedestrian season so far. His numbers are down from 2025 in completion percentage (64.3 to 59.9), yards per attempt (6.4 to 5.8) and passer rating (87.8 to 80.8). The Broncos rank 30th in total offense after being 10th last season.

Nix, though, doesn't see it that way.

“Playing good and playing bad, it’s a narrative, and I think it’s honestly kind of something we make up,” Nix said after Tuesday’s practice, via Chris Tomasson of The Denver Gazette. “I don’t think necessarily I’m playing any different than what I’m normally playing.”

Nix was only 16-of-27 for 123 yards with a touchdown in Sunday's 23-17 win over the Chargers. He had only one completion longer than 16 yards.

Nix, though, looks at the positive.

“We’re sitting here at 3-2 and having a good start to our season,” Nix said. “There’s things we want to clean up. There’s things we want to fix. We’re leaving some things out there on the field but we’re finding ways to win like we did last year [during a 14-3 season]. I feel strongly that we’re going to continue to do that.”

item.title: Sean McVay gives special teams coach Bubba Ventrone vote of confidence
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Rams' special teams miscues cost kicker Harrison Mevis his job.
item.content:encoded:
The Rams' special teams miscues cost kicker Harrison Mevis his job. It won't cost special teams coach Bubba Ventrone his.

Rams head coach Sean McVay said Tuesday that Ventrone's job is safe.

“I have a lot of confidence in Bubba Ventrone," McVay said, via NFL.com. "There’s no changes that are gonna be made there. We’re gonna keep working. This isn’t the first time that we’ve had adversity and the first time that we’ve had some different things that I have to do a better job of.”

The Rams fired special teams coordinator Chase Blackburn in December after a series of blunders by the unit in a 38-37 overtime loss to the Seahawks. Assistant special teams coach Ben Kotwica finished the season as the interim coordinator, but the Rams muffed a punt in the NFC Championship Game.

The Rams hired Ventrone in January.

He was the assistant head coach and special teams coordinator for three seasons on Cleveland’s staff. He has also coached for the Colts and Patriots since concluding a playing career that saw him spend time with the 49ers, Browns and Patriots.

Ventrone inherited Mevis, who went 12-of-13 on field goals and made all his extra points last season.

Mevis missed two field goals in the Rams' 37-34 overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night. He was wide left on a 50-yard try on the Rams' first possession and had a 48-yard, game-winning attempt blocked by Greg Rousseau in overtime.

Mevis had missed four of nine attempts this season.

The Rams signed kicker Blake Grupe off the Jets' practice squad on Tuesday.

item.title: Chargers agree to terms with QB Jake Browning
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: With Trey Lance on injured reserve with a groin injury, the Chargers needed quarterback help.
item.content:encoded:
With Trey Lance on injured reserve with a groin injury, the Chargers needed quarterback help.

They worked out quarterbacks Jake Browning and Kyle Trask, along with cornerback Jalyn Armour-Davis, wide receiver Ronnie Bell, wide receiver Luke Grimm, wide receiver Chris Hilton, wide receiver Tejhaun Palmer and wide receiver JuJu Smith-Schuster.

They signed Grimm to the practice squad, and Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports that the team has come to terms with Browning. It is unclear whether Browning is signing with the practice squad or the active roster.

Justin Herbert and DJ Uiagalelei are the only quarterbacks on the 53-player roster.

Browning, 30, was with the Bengals the past four seasons before joining the Bucs in free agency this offseason. Tampa Bay cut him out of the preseason.

He has appeared in 17 games with 10 starts and has completed 68.5 percent of his passes for 2,707 yards with 18 touchdowns and 15 interceptions.
